dse_runs.notes: Tight accuracy spec: max_abs_err <= 2^-20 (~9.54e-07) AND throughput >= 50 MSPS simultaneously. Search the whole data-width range aggressively (high width needed to meet 2^-20; check where err saturates) and prefer families/structures that reach 50 MSPS without massive unroll cost: pipelined with modest stages and unrolled_k may both qualify. Keep the front well spread on luts_plus_ffs vs power_index; do not let the front collapse to only ultra-wide designs. Selection rule is min luts_plus_ffs, so keep many feasible low-area points, but cover the power end too.

final_text: The campaign queue held a single spec, `high_precision` (coherent demodulator: max_abs_err ≤ 2^-20 ≈ 9.53674e-07 at throughput ≥ 50 MSPS, minimising luts_plus_ffs and power_index, selected by min luts_plus_ffs). I spent the full L1 budget (400/400) on the structured DSE graph — the inner architect mapped the front three times then stopped, returning exactly one non-dominated feasible design, `pipelined_m:data_width=26,n_iter=22,angle_guard=2,frac_guard=0,rounding=round,m=7` (estimates: luts_plus_ffs=2312, luts=1908, ffs=404, power_index=4.35, throughput 52 MSPS, max_abs_err 6.89e-07 = 2^-20.47, both constraints met with the accuracy margin coming from the 26-bit width and the throughput from a modest m=7 stage count). L2 `simulate_system` found no system scenario, so it supplied contract facts (6-cycle latency, one sample/cycle) and simulated DDS quality (SFDR 141.5 dBc, SNR 130.6 dB) without changing the selection; L3 `verify_rtl` and L4 `synthesize` had no recorded rows for this configuration and L5 `back_annotate` returned `no_measured_data`, so no WINNER CHANGE was flagged and `reexplore` was correctly skipped. The spec is finalized on that design, which is feasible on L1/L2 estimates but carries the explicit caveat that it is unverified at RTL and unsynthesized (only the generator, not this configuration, has RTL verification coverage). Finally, `remember` had no effect: memory is switched off for this campaign, so no lesson was stored; `recall` at the start likewise returned nothing, meaning this run had no prior-campaign calibration to lean on.
